rationale: The literature confirms a genotype-phenotype correlation in DHX9, where loss-of-function (LoF) variants generally result in milder neurodevelopmental disorder (NDD) phenotypes compared to certain missense variants. However, detailed functional and quantitative HPO analyses reveal that severe NDD is specifically linked to nuclear localization signal (NLS) missense variants (which lead to cytoplasmic accumulation) and specific R-loop-increasing variants (e.g., p.Arg141Gln), rather than helicase or nucleotide-binding domain variants per se. Missense variants in the helicase/conserved regions frequently cause axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2 (CMT2) with aberrant nucleolar accumulation, and ATP-binding site variants (such as p.Gly414Arg) have been characterized functionally as loss-of-function rather than dominant-negative.

evidence.text: Quantitative HPO analysis identified 20 individuals with de novo DHX9 variants and demonstrated genotype-phenotype correlations where LoF variants cause mild NDD, whereas nuclear localization signal (NLS) missense variants cause severe NDD characterized by cytoplasmic accumulation. In contrast, missense variants causing axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (CMT2) led to aberrant nucleolar accumulation, and ATPase domain variants showed altered enzymatic activity without driving the classic severe NDD phenotype linked to NLS disruptions.

source.title: Monoallelic variation in DHX9, the gene encoding the DExH-box helicase DHX9, underlies neurodevelopment disorders and Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease
source.journal: The American Journal of Human Genetics
source.quote: Quantitative Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) analysis demonstrated genotype-phenotype correlations with LoF variants causing mild NDD phenotypes and nuclear localization signal (NLS) missense variants causing severe NDD.

evidence.text: Characterization of a de novo missense variant directly within the glycine codon of the conserved ATP-binding domain (p.Gly414Arg) in a patient with intellectual disability, short stature, and cardiomyopathy demonstrated through Drosophila and mouse models that this variant behaves as a loss-of-function allele, rather than causing a severe dominant-negative effect.

source.title: Heterozygous loss-of-function DHX9 variants are associated with neurodevelopmental disorders: Human genetic and experimental evidences
source.quote: In conclusion, we established that heterozygosity for a loss-of-function variant of DHX9 can lead to a new neurodevelopmental disorder.

evidence.text: Monoallelic de novo loss-of-function and missense variants in DHX9 and related DEAD/DEAH-box RNA helicases show genotype-phenotype correlations, confirming that variant class and domain positioning dictate whether clinical manifestation presents as mild NDD, severe NDD, or neuropathy.

conflicts: Severe NDD is driven specifically by NLS (nuclear localization signal) missense variants that result in cytoplasmic mislocalization and by N-terminal dsRBD variants (e.g., p.Arg141Gln) causing R-loop accumulation, rather than missense variants clustered generally across the conserved helicase/nucleotide-binding domains.

Missense variants within the nucleotide-binding motif (such as p.Gly414Arg) have been experimentally characterized as causing loss-of-function/haploinsufficiency rather than dominant-negative interference.

Conserved helicase core missense variants are frequently associated with axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (CMT2) and nucleolar stress accumulation rather than the most severe syndromic NDD phenotypes.

new_directions.question_text: Does subcellular partitioning (nuclear vs. cytoplasmic vs. nucleolar accumulation) quantitatively predict clinical severity and distinguish NDD from CMT2 across an expanded DHX9 cohort?
new_directions.rationale: Calame et al. showed distinct cellular localizations correlating with clinical divergence (NLS variants in cytoplasm -> severe NDD; CMT2 variants in nucleolus; LoF in nucleus). A systematic cellular localization screen of novel variants could provide a prospective diagnostic and prognostic biomarker.

new_directions.question_text: Do helicase-domain missense variants exert dominant-negative inhibition on wild-type DHX9 unwinding complexes, or do they act primarily as hypomorphic/null alleles in vivo?
new_directions.rationale: Yamada et al. concluded p.Gly414Arg acts as loss-of-function, whereas other helicase paralogs (e.g., DHX30) operate via severe dominant-negative mechanisms. Testing biochemical unwinding and multimeric interactions in co-expression models will settle the mechanistic classification.
